{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from PBS
# CRITICAL: This script is a template. Placeholders like '{{:ncpus}}' must be
# filled in before submission.
#FLUX: -n {{:ncpus}}
#FLUX: -t {{:wallhr}}:00:00
#FLUX: -q normal

#
# --- Omitted PBS options and explanations ---
#
# -P np01
#   Omitted. Flux accounting is typically managed through system configuration or job
#   submission options, not a standard batch directive.
#
# -N "{{:name}}"
#   Omitted. The job name in Flux is generally set during submission (e.g.,
#   'flux submit --job-name=... ...') or via the FLUX_JOB_NAME
#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#
# -l mem={{:mem}}GB
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a direct batch script directive for memory.
#   Performance implication: Without a memory constraint, the job may be
#   scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, potentially causing it to
#   fail with an out-of-memory error or perform poorly due to heavy swapping.
#
# -j oe
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into a single output file by default
#   when no error file (-e) is specified. If an output file is specified with -o,
#   both streams will go to it. This matches the requested behavior.
#

source $HOME/hpc-environments/gadi/load-intel.sh
PROJECT_DIR=$SCRATCH/{{:dir_name}}/

# 'mpiexec' is replaced by 'flux run'. 'flux run' will automatically use the
# number of tasks specified by the '#FLUX: -n' directive.
flux run julia --project=$PROJECT_DIR --check-bounds no -O3 \
    $PROJECT_DIR/scripts/Benchmarks/benchmark_gadi.jl \
    {{:name}} \
    {{{:write_dir}}} \
    {{:type}} \
    {{:bmark_type}} \
    {{:Nx_partition}} \
    {{:Ny_partition}} \
    {{:Nz_partition}} \
    {{:n_el_size}} \
    {{:fe_order}} \
    {{:verbose}} \
    {{:nreps}}
"
}
